title: Judge PRs by required checks; let held-job records pass head check
summary: Fix two blockers for drain landings, for the maintainer running the drain. (1) The drain judges a pull request only by the required check ("fmt, clippy, tests"), so a red optional check such as the pull request head check is a note, not a failure. (2) The pre-merge classification no longer returns NoVerification for a held job's records, while a finished job's closing records without verification still fail.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new drain and invariant tests and passing cargo test, clippy, fmt.
Criteria check outcomes (landed or waiting report, pass or fail of the head check) through named tests.
Judge by required checks generally, and classify held jobs by their records, not one instance.
Both rules are enforced in code and tests, not prose.
One focused change covering the two stated problems.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs (PrHost::checks at ~405 calls classify_checks at ~766, which turns any failed check-run into Checks::Red and has no notion of required names; CI_AGGREGATE_JOB = "fmt, clippy, tests" at ~516), crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs (EARLY_RUN_JOB), crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs (~169-340, the landing wait and the 'checks red' standing text), and crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs (closing_jobs ~234, Uncovered::NoVerification ~278, classify_pre_merge ~311, which returns NoVerification when a job's closing records lack verification.json). The entry points are the landing wait in gh/landing.rs and classify_pre_merge; the producer must locate how the drain maps Red to 'not landed' and the repeated-failure stop.

The required-check name set is what main requires: the single job named 'fmt, clippy, tests' (see xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs REQUIRED_CHECK_NAME). The producer should reuse that existing constant or recorded name instead of adding a second list; optional checks (the pull request head, attribution of main) are ignored when judging red, and appear only as a note.

A 'held job' is one whose state is a low-disk hold (crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, state.rs). The invariant fix must identify it from the job's own records in the commit tree (for example a hold record present and no outcome or candidate record), so a finished job (candidate or outcome records) without verification still yields NoVerification.

No record or data file is added under crates/, so the records validation allow-list (check_record_file, AnyRecord round-trip) is not touched, unless the producer finds the hold marker is a new record kind, which this reading does not expect.
The change adds no new refusal; it narrows two existing ones, so the replay refusal rate should fall. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.
Governance: .github/workflows/ci.yml, athena.toml and defaults.toml need no change; the 'not yet required' marking stays as is.

acceptance_criteria.text: A drain/gh test (cargo test -p athena-core) where the required check 'fmt, clippy, tests' is green and an optional check (the pull request head) is red reports landed or waiting, never failed, and the run does not stop for a repeated failure.
A drain test (cargo test -p athena-core) shows that a red required check is still reported as failed, and a pending required check stays waiting, so the behavior is not weakened.

An invariant test (cargo test -p athena-gate) shows a commit adding a held job's records with no verification passes classify_pre_merge (no Uncovered::NoVerification), and a commit adding a finished job's closing records with no verification still returns NoVerification.
The red-optional-check case is surfaced as a note in the drain or landing output (visible in the test's assertion on the report), not as the 'not landed: pull request is Open, checks Red' error.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that describes both fixes (required-checks-only judgment, held-job records pass the pull request head check).
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check pass for the workspace.
The required check names are taken from one existing source (the 'fmt, clippy, tests' constant in the code), and not duplicated as an unrelated second list; verified by Grep of the diff.
Expected 0% of newly refused readings: the change only narrows refusals, so the higher refusal rate is not intended.

out_of_scope: Making the pull request head check required, or editing .github/workflows/ci.yml
Changing the disk-hold logic itself or the low-disk threshold
Changes to the drain's thrash-stop rule for genuine repeated failures
Changes to records/ or branch-protection settings on GitHub
departures: Two interacting fixes in gate-like code with unclear required-name sourcing and held-job detection; slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: the drain stops runs on a repeated false landing failure, and held jobs' records are refused by the head check.
hard_reason: Changes the landing gate (how checks judge a pull request) and the pre-merge records rule that can refuse a commit, so a mistake could let bad landings through or keep refusing good ones.
